newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso defensive,C. Bank may intervene.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso defensive,C. Bank may intervene.

text.p: The Philippine peso could see continued weakness on Wednesday as banks remain cautious over possible dollar outflows due to the slump in the local equities market, traders said.
The Philippine Central Bank, however, is expected to curb the peso's fall, they added.
The peso closed at 26.37 on Tuesday from 26.369.
"Because of the sales of foreign fund mangers (in the stock market), some may bring their dollars out of the country," a foreign bank dealer said.
"The Central Bank is still offering dollars at 26.37. So, the peso should remain stable," another trader said.
"We'll probaly see some outflows but probably not that significant," he added.
He believed foreign fund managers would stay in the country and are just waiting for better prices before investing again in the stock market.
The stock market tumbled to a two-year low on Tuesday due to fears of a correction in the property market and disappointing first quarter earnings of blue chip issues.
